tasks.short: Set and maintain a bank and table limit for each game.

steps.what: Set and maintain a bank and table limit for each game.

tasks.design: The gambling manager sets the cash bank and the table limit for each game on the floor. That limit is the act. No second posting of the limit is removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: A limit set too high is money the house can lose on that game, and only someone on the floor sees the crowd.
tasks.enabler_now: Class human and a records-app score are priors. The digest's policy libraries, shift planning, and incident registers cover other management tasks. They do not set this house's bank and table limit, so this task stays as it is.
tasks.still_hard: The right bank and table limit for this game, on this night.
tasks.human_edge: Standing behind the limit for that game.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The gambling manager still sets the cash bank and the table limit for each game on the floor.

reach.role: Entertainment and Recreation Managers, Except Gambling
reach.task: Set a cash float and a spending cap for an event
reach.learn: Learn how that manager sets a cash float and a spending cap from the crowd at the event.

evidence.claim: Setting a cash bank and a table limit for each game is the gambling manager's own floor decision. Policy libraries, shift planning, and incident registers for other management tasks do not set that limit.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the gambling manager sets the cash bank and the table limit for each game on the floor. No structured feed is added, so there is no new field and no producer. If the floor is quiet she still sets the limit from the house rules and the crowd she sees. Manual fallback is that the person continues as now.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
unknowns: Whether this house posts the same limit into a second book after she sets it on the floor.
research_questions: Does this house post the same table limit into a second book after the gambling manager sets it on the floor?

already_counted.description: Setting the cash bank and the table limit on the floor remains in this step.

incremental.description: No template, mapping, or list is kept. Upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The gambling manager still sets the cash bank and the table limit on the floor. No second posting of the limit goes away. A conservative case is a night of table limits set in person, so the low stays at zero.

tasks.short: Direct compilation of summary sheets of wager amounts and payoffs.

steps.what: Direct the compilation of summary sheets for races or events.
Read wager amounts and payoffs on the summary sheets.

tasks.design: The gambling manager still names which races or events to compile and still reads the wager amounts and payoffs on the summary sheets. This statement does not establish a second writing of those amounts. The sheets stay the compilation she directs.
tasks.previous_blocker: A summary that misstates payoffs is a financial error, and the manager is accountable for which races or events are included.
tasks.enabler_now: Class automate and an artefact score are priors. The digest's report pattern covers other management tasks. It does not establish that this manager retypes wager lines onto the summary sheets, so directing the compilation and reading the amounts stay as they are.
tasks.still_hard: Whether these sheets include the right races or events and the right payoffs.
tasks.human_edge: Naming which races or events to compile, and standing behind the amounts she reads.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still directs which races or events to compile and still reads the wager amounts and payoffs.

reach.learn: Learn how a spa manager names which treatments to total and then reads the amounts.

evidence.claim: Directing which races or events to compile, and reading wager amounts and payoffs on the summary sheets, is the gambling manager's own work. Report tools for other management tasks do not name those races or stand behind those amounts.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the gambling manager names which races or events to compile and then reads the wager amounts and payoffs on the summary sheets. No structured feed is added, so there is no new field and no producer. The sheets stay the compilation she directs. If a total is missing she still asks staff and still reads what they bring. Manual fallback is that the person continues as now.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
unknowns: Whether staff retype each wager line onto the summary sheets after the bet is already in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, or the sheets already come from that system.
research_questions: Do staff retype each wager line onto the summary sheets after the bet is already in the {OPS_SYSTEM}?

incremental.description: No template, mapping, or list is kept. Upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still names which races or events to compile and still reads the wager amounts and payoffs on the summary sheets. This statement does not establish a second writing of those amounts. A conservative case is a day of race summaries she still directs and reads, so the low stays at zero.

tasks.short: Review expenses, budgets, betting accounts, and collection reports for accuracy.

steps.what: Compare matching lines on operational expenses, budget estimates, betting accounts, and collection reports.
Review those figures and judge accuracy.

tasks.design: A configured comparison on the {ERP} and the {OPS_SYSTEM} marks lines that already agree across operational expenses, budget estimates, betting accounts, and collection reports. The gambling manager still reviews the figures and judges accuracy. Lines that do not agree, and any report that is not in those systems, stay with her.
tasks.previous_blocker: A wrong accuracy call on expenses, betting accounts, or collections is a financial error.
tasks.enabler_now: Class automate and a records-app score are priors. The digest's budget pattern covers other management tasks and is not proof this manager retypes these reports. The scan of lines that already agree is part of this accuracy review, and a configured comparison can mark those lines. The accuracy call stays with her.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the figures that do not agree are still accurate.
tasks.human_edge: The call that the reports are or are not accurate.
tasks.altitude: The tick-through of lines that already agree can be marked for her. She still judges accuracy. No decision right moves.

reach.task: Review class revenue against the budget
reach.learn: Learn how a coordinator judges which class-revenue mismatches against the budget are real.

evidence.claim: Reviewing operational expenses, budget estimates, betting accounts, and collection reports for accuracy is the gambling manager's own call. A configured comparison can mark lines that already agree. It does not judge the lines that do not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the finance team already keeps operational expenses and budget estimates in the {ERP}, and cashiers already keep betting accounts and collection reports in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Those records are existing runtime. No new field is added. The comparison only marks lines that already agree. If a report is not in those systems, the gambling manager compares it by hand. Manual fallback is that the person continues as now.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
unknowns: Whether those reports for this house arrive only on paper.
research_questions: Do operational expenses, budget estimates, betting accounts, and collection reports for this house arrive only on paper?

already_counted.description: The accuracy judgement remains in the review step.

incremental.description: No template, mapping, or list is kept. Upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When a report arrives only on paper, the comparison does not run and she reviews every line herself, so the low stays at zero. The high is the scan of lines that already agree when the reports are already in the {ERP} and the {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.short: Record bets, collect stakes, pay winners, and issue receipts.

steps.what: Record each bet at the window.
At the window, collect the stake or pay off the bet.
Hand the receipt, issuing receipts as necessary.

tasks.design: She records each bet in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, takes the stake or pays the winner at the window, and hands the receipt from that same bet entry. No second writing of the bet is removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paying the wrong winner or taking the wrong stake is hard to undo at the window.
tasks.enabler_now: Class human and a records-app score are priors. The digest's records pattern covers other management tasks. It does not take a stake or pay a winner at this window, so recording, collecting, and issuing the receipt stay as they are.
tasks.still_hard: The person, the stake, and the payoff in front of her.
tasks.human_edge: Taking the cash and paying the winner herself.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still records the bet, takes the stake or pays the winner, and hands the receipt.

reach.learn: Learn how that manager takes a ticket payment and hands the receipt at the door.

evidence.claim: Recording a bet, taking the stake or paying the winner, and handing the receipt are the gambling manager's own acts at the window. A records app does not take the cash or pay the winner.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the gambling manager records each bet in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, takes the stake or pays the winner at the window, and hands the receipt from that same bet entry. No new field is added. If the window system is down she writes the bet by hand and still takes the cash. Manual fallback is that the person continues as now.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
unknowns: Whether this window writes the same bet again after the receipt is handed to the bettor.
